typical_topologies: point-to-point interconnect standardized by the InfiniBand Trade
InfiniBand is a serial, differential, point-to-point physical link.

id_routing.description: Interconnect may append bits to AxID to identify the originating master; slave-side ID_WIDTH > master-side ID_WIDTH
id_routing.compliance_note: Returning ID is the WIDER value; routing strips appended bits before returning to the master

fields.topology_type: Switched fabric. End nodes (Channel Adapters) connect to switches; switches forward within a subnet by LID; routers join subnets and forward by GID. Each subnet is owned by a Subnet Manager that assigns 16-bit LIDs. Common physical topologies are fat-tree / Clos and torus.

supported_topologies.name: Single subnet
supported_topologies.description: Channel Adapters + switches managed by one Subnet Manager (LID forwarding).

supported_topologies.name: Multi-subnet
supported_topologies.description: Subnets joined by routers; GID (128-bit) inter-subnet routing.

supported_topologies.name: Fat-tree / Clos
supported_topologies.description: Non-blocking multi-stage switch fabric for HPC.

supported_topologies.name: Torus / mesh
supported_topologies.description: Direct switch topology for large clusters.

master_slave_role_summary.description: Host end node; verbs interface; originates/terminates RDMA + SEND/RECEIVE.
I/O end node; device-specific I/O Controller interface.
Assigns LIDs; programs forwarding tables; owns the subnet.

fields.interconnect_role: InfiniBand is a switched, channel-based fabric. The Link Layer moves packets hop-by-hop within a subnet (LID, per-VL credits, VCRC); the Network Layer routes between subnets (GID); the Transport Layer delivers messages end-to-end over Queue Pairs with PSN-based reliability for RC/RD.

ordering_guarantees.packet_sequence: PSN orders packets within a message on a reliable QP.
ordering_guarantees.vl_arbitration: VL arbitration shares the link fairly; SL-to-VL mapping isolates traffic classes.
ordering_guarantees.unreliable: UC/UD give no delivery/ordering guarantee beyond a single packet/MTU.

fields.memory_vs_peripheral_regions: InfiniBand transports messages, not a memory map; RDMA targets a registered Memory Region addressed by virtual address + R_Key on the remote node. Fabric addressing is LID (subnet) / GID (global) / QPN (node).
